model_note: New Talisman Gold Mines Limited (NTL.NZ) is NOT a growth-DCF candidate. It is a pre-commercial, single-asset gold/silver explorer transitioning toward small-scale production, with a FULL DISCLAIMER OF AUDIT OPINION on its FY2025 and FY2026 financial statements (Baker Tilly Staples Rodway could not obtain sufficient evidence on the recoverable amount of the ~NZ$15.6m Talisman Mine cash-generating unit, which is the vast majority of the balance sheet), explicit going-concern uncertainty, negative owner FCF in every fiscal year on record (FY2018-FY2026), first-ever gold concentrate revenue in FY2026 that was insufficient to cover costs, a persistent 8-year pattern of dilutive equity raises (shares on issue grew from ~2.16bn pre-consolidation-equivalent bases through repeated placements/rights issues to 793,346,782 as of the FY2026 annual report), and an ASX secondary-listing suspension since June 2024. There is no repeatable, positive free-cash-flow series to project and no meaningful terminal growth rate to discount - a conventional owner-FCF DCF would either extrapolate a business that has never existed (sustained positive FCF) or compound an unrepeatable cash-burn trajectory into a nonsensical negative-infinity valuation. This mirrors the structural approach used for the comparable NZX distressed/going-concern-risk names AFC.NZ and BGI.NZ (research/AFC.NZ/Reports/AFC.NZ_DCF.json, research/BGI.NZ/Reports/BGI.NZ_DCF.json), adapted for NTL.NZ's specific facts: unlike those two dormant cash shells, NTL.NZ retains a genuine, JORC-classified 350,000 oz gold-equivalent resource at ~17 g/t grade, a commissioned processing plant, and signed offtake agreements (Ocean Partners UK for concentrate, Melody Gold for low-grade ore/tailings) - i.e. real, if unproven, asset optionality on top of the going-concern risk, rather than a pure shell/RTO-option value. The model therefore blends (a) a failure/wind-down waterfall (bear), (b) a muddle-through scenario where the company continues to fund itself via dilutive capital raises (its unbroken 8-year pattern) while never scaling production to real profitability (base), and (c) a successful-ramp scenario where narrow-vein execution is solved and the resource is partially monetized via an EV/resource-ounce approach consistent with junior-miner precedent (bull).

inputs.shares_outstanding_note: 793,346,782 shares on issue per the FY2026 Annual Report (year ended 31-Mar-2026), which already includes the 8-Apr-2026 shortfall placement of 1,740,063 shares from the March-2026 4-for-5 rights offer. This is more current than the Metrics.csv FY2026 column (791,606,719, pre-shortfall-placement) and is used here as the freshest available fully-issued count. Note: FY2023 was preceded by a 10:1 share consolidation, breaking comparability of any pre-FY2023 per-share history.
inputs.net_debt_note: Total debt NZ$93,133 less cash NZ$1,176,627 (both FY2026, 31-Mar-2026 balance sheet) = net CASH of NZ$1,083,494. This is a NET-CASH position, but the cash balance is small relative to the company's own stated ongoing capital needs and burn rate, and is NOT treated as a source of distributable value on top of the scenario equity values below - it is already embedded inside the FY2026 shareholders' equity figure (NZ$16,977,146) used as the base/bear anchor, so it is not subtracted or added a second time.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026 reported free cash flow (OCF -1,967,666 + CapEx -979,157). Shown for disclosure only - there is no repeatable owner-FCF base to project. Every fiscal year FY2018-FY2026 has produced negative FCF; the company has never generated a positive free-cash-flow year in its disclosed history.
inputs.sbc_source: Metrics.csv StockBasedComp column is 0 for every period FY2018-FY2026; no share-based payment expense has ever been disclosed. No SBC adjustment is required (the entire valuation problem here is going-concern/execution risk and equity dilution via cash raises, not share-based compensation).
inputs.annual_share_growth_note: Not a flat/SBC-driven dilution rate. NTL.NZ's dilution comes entirely from CASH capital raises (rights issues and private placements), which the company itself says will continue ('further capital will be required to fully implement all phases' of the strategic plan). The base case models a declining-but-persistent annual dilution path of 18%/15%/12%/8%/5% over 5 years (cumulative ~72% share count growth), consistent with the unbroken 8-year raise history (shares grew from ~625m Sep-2024 to ~793m Mar-2026, i.e. roughly +27% in 18 months). See assumptions.base.dilution_path.
inputs.share_count_basis: 793,346,782 actual shares on issue per FY2026 Annual Report (incl. 8-Apr-2026 shortfall placement). Forward dilution modelled explicitly per scenario (see projected_shares_*) because further capital raises are a near-certainty in the base case and a stated company dependency, NOT held flat - this is genuine non-SBC dilution (cash raises), the opposite of the SBC-flat-share-count convention used for operating companies.
inputs.units: absolute dollars (not thousands or millions) in narrative/equity figures except shares_outstanding and net_debt, which are stated in millions/thousands as labelled above, per Metrics.csv convention
inputs.talisman_cgu_note: The consolidated FY2026 balance sheet includes net assets of NZ$15,583,116 attributed to the Talisman Mine cash-generating unit (CGU) - roughly 92% of total shareholders' equity of NZ$16,977,146. The auditor (Baker Tilly Staples Rodway) issued a DISCLAIMER OF OPINION - the second consecutive year - specifically because it could not obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence on the recoverable amount of this CGU, in particular the amount of gold to be recovered, future gold prices, and future cash flows arising from the project. This is the single largest driver of scenario dispersion in this model: the base and bear cases apply material haircuts to this carrying value precisely because the auditor itself could not verify it.
inputs.audit_opinion_note: Second consecutive year of a full DISCLAIMER OF OPINION (not merely a qualified opinion or going-concern emphasis-of-matter) - materially more severe, meaning the auditor could not obtain sufficient evidence to form ANY opinion on the Talisman Mine CGU's recoverable amount.
inputs.asx_suspension: suspended June 2024 for inadequate financial condition; NZX primary listing (NTL.NZ) remains active with periodic trading halts around material announcements (most recently Oct-Nov 2025 around the first concentrate shipment)
inputs.first_production_note: FY2026 saw first-ever gold concentrate revenue (Ocean Partners UK offtake) and low-grade ore/tailings revenue (Melody Gold), totaling NZ$52,790 against operating + admin costs of ~NZ$2.27m - i.e. revenue covered roughly 2% of costs. First concentrate shipment (announced 19-Nov-2025) realised a lower grade than planned, generating only US$21.7k. Management has since paused further mine development in favour of geological modelling and targeted drilling (strategic reset, per FY2026 annual report).
inputs.notes: Model: asset/scenario-weighted valuation (probability-weighted mix of failure/wind-down, muddle-through-with-dilution, and successful-ramp scenarios), NOT a growth owner-FCF DCF. Routed per .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md 'Distressed, receivership, delisted, cash shell -> Asset or creditor waterfall - not a going-concern model' row, adapted here because NTL.NZ (unlike AFC.NZ/BGI.NZ) is not yet a dormant shell - it has a real JORC resource, commissioned plant and offtake agreements, so the bull case values genuine (if unproven) production optionality via an EV/resource-ounce approach rather than pure listed-shell scarcity value. Rationale for departing from a standard owner-FCF DCF: (1) FCF has been negative in all 9 disclosed fiscal years FY2018-FY2026 with no positive year to establish a base or trend; (2) the auditor's disclaimer of opinion means even the reported book-equity anchor (NZ$16,977,146) cannot be taken as reliably verified without applying an independent haircut; (3) the company itself discloses that further capital is required with no assurance it will be available - i.e. continued existence is contingent on dilutive financing events that a cash-flow-discounting framework cannot represent.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Not applicable in the conventional growth-DCF sense, but flagged for a different reason: revenue CAGRs (102.7% 3yr, 77.8% 5yr) look explosive purely because they compound off a near-zero base (FY2021 revenue NZ$2,973; FY2023 NZ$6,340) toward FY2026's still-tiny NZ$52,790 - this is NOT evidence of a scaling, repeatable business; it is the statistical artifact of dividing a small number by an even smaller one. FCF CAGR is null/not meaningful because FCF has been negative in every year of the series (no valid compounding base). Equity CAGR (16.3% 3yr, 2.2% 5yr) is positive only because of large, dilutive capital raises being booked directly into contributed equity, offsetting years of accumulated losses - it reflects shareholders paying in more cash, not the business compounding intrinsic value. None of these series is used to drive a forward growth projection; see growth_rate_source.
historical_growth.notes: No meaningful growth-rate driver exists for a conventional DCF. Revenue growth is off a near-zero base and driven by the first-ever, currently loss-making production ramp, not an established trend. FCF has never been positive. Equity growth is dilution-funded, not earnings-compounded. This is precisely why the valuation below abandons growth-rate selection in favour of a probability-weighted asset/scenario model, consistent with the AFC.NZ and BGI.NZ precedents in this research folder.

base.narrative: The company continues its unbroken 8-year pattern of funding itself through dilutive capital raises (rights issues and private placements), consistent with management's own disclosure that 'further capital will be required to fully implement all phases' of the revised strategic plan. Development is paused near-term in favour of geological modelling and targeted drilling at Mystery, Dubbo, Crown/Welcome and the new Rahu permit, per the FY2027 guidance. Production remains sub-scale and does not durably cover cash costs within the 5-year horizon - the narrow-vein execution problems that caused FY2026's shortfall (unpredictable orebody orientation, lower-than-planned concentrate grade) are only partially resolved. Existing shareholders' claim is valued against today's asset base (FY2026 book equity), with the Talisman Mine CGU haircut to reflect the auditor's inability to verify its recoverable amount, and diluted forward by the capital-raise path the company itself signals is coming.
base.cgu_haircut_note: 40% haircut to the NZ$15,583,116 Talisman Mine CGU carrying value. Chosen as a middle-of-range judgment: less severe than the near-total haircut applied in the bear/wind-down case (where a forced-sale/liquidation discount applies), but material enough to reflect that the auditor issued a full disclaimer - not merely a qualification - specifically on this asset's recoverability, for the second consecutive year, and that the one operating year of actual production data (FY2026) has so far undershot plan.
base.dilution_path_note: Annual share-count growth from continued cash raises, front-loaded (reflecting the near-certainty of near-term funding given the current NZ$1.18m cash balance against ongoing burn) and tapering as the strategic-reset drilling program (if it shows results) reduces reliance on emergency financing. Cumulative dilution over 5 years: ~72% (793.3m -> ~1,367.6m shares). No proceeds from these future raises are added back to the equity numerator - conservative, since FY2026 showed that incremental cash funds ongoing burn rather than growing net asset value at a rate that outpaces dilution.
base.discounting_note: No projectable free-cash-flow stream exists to discount to a present value (negative FCF in all 9 disclosed fiscal years, no positive base year). Value is instead assessed as a probability-weighted claim on today's (haircut) net asset value, diluted forward for expected future capital raises - an NTA/dilution model, not a discounted cash flow.

bull.narrative: Geological modelling and targeted drilling (Mystery, Dubbo, Crown/Welcome, Rahu) successfully de-risk the resource and resolve the narrow-vein orientation problems that caused FY2026's production shortfall. The commissioned processing plant and existing Ocean Partners/Melody Gold offtake agreements are utilised at a rate that generates sustained positive cash flow within the horizon, converting the 350,000 oz AuEq JORC resource into genuine production economics. This scenario does NOT assume the company becomes a large, low-cost producer - it assumes the narrower, more probable success case of validating the emerging-producer thesis at small scale, which is valued via an EV-per-resource-ounce approach consistent with junior/emerging-producer precedent, rather than a discounted cash-flow build of a hypothetical mine plan that the company itself has not disclosed (no reserve statement, no mine plan, no production target exists in current disclosure).
bull.ev_per_oz_note: US$40/oz applied to the 350,000 oz AuEq JORC resource. This sits toward the lower-middle of the typical US$25-100/oz range junior gold explorers/emerging producers command once a processing plant is commissioned and first sales have occurred (vs. US$10-25/oz for pure pre-production explorers with no plant/offtake, and US$60-150+/oz for producers with a demonstrated, scaling production rate) - i.e. it credits NTL.NZ for having cleared the 'plant commissioned + offtake signed' milestones (which it has) without assuming it has yet cleared the 'demonstrated scalable production' milestone (which FY2026 showed it has not).
bull.dilution_path_note: Lighter, front-loaded dilution (two further raises to fund the drilling/de-risking program, ~27% cumulative) versus the base case, reflecting that a successful, funded drilling result would reduce the company's reliance on emergency dilutive financing relative to the base case's continued struggle.

bear.narrative: Production ramp fails to improve from FY2026's shortfall (narrow-vein execution problems persist or worsen), the strategic-reset drilling program does not resolve the resource-continuity uncertainty within a survivable timeframe, and the company's cash position (NZ$1.18m at FY2026 year-end against negative operating cash flow of ~NZ$2.0m/year) is exhausted before further capital can be raised or on acceptable terms. The going-concern uncertainty crystallizes into insolvency/forced wind-down. In this outcome, the Talisman Mine CGU - the asset the auditor could not verify - realizes only a small fraction of its carrying value in a forced sale of a single-asset, illiquid, narrow-vein underground mining permit (there is no established market of buyers for a distressed micro-cap NZ gold permit at short notice), and ordinary equity holders receive a small residual after wind-down costs, remaining liabilities and the (already-small) debt balance are settled.
bear.cgu_recovery_note: 10% recovery on the NZ$15,583,116 CGU carrying value in a forced liquidation - reflecting that mining permits/exploration assets typically realize only a small fraction of book value in distressed, time-pressured sales, especially where (as here) the auditor itself could not verify the underlying recoverable-amount assumptions (gold recovery rates, future prices, future cash flows).
bear.wind_down_costs_note: Provision for liquidator/administrator costs, environmental/rehabilitation obligations crystallizing faster than the existing NZ$452,599 provision covers, and other wind-down expenses.
bear.no_further_dilution: Assumes no further capital raises complete once the going-concern failure crystallizes (share count held at the current 793.3m) - a company failing outright does not get further dilutive-but-value-preserving financing rounds; it winds down.

base.note: No forward revenue/FCF projection is built - FY2026 first-production revenue (NZ$52,790) covered roughly 2% of costs and management has issued no quantitative production/revenue guidance for FY2027 or beyond (guidance is explicitly qualitative: pause development, prioritize drilling/geological modelling). Projecting a specific revenue/FCF path would fabricate precision the company's own disclosure does not support. Value is instead assessed via the haircut-NTA-plus-dilution approach in the valuation section.

bull.note: Only the terminal EV/oz asset value is modelled (see assumptions.bull) - no interim cash-flow path is projected for the same reason as the base case: no disclosed mine plan or production target exists.

bear.note: Wind-down assumed to crystallize within FY2027 once cash runway (NZ$1.18m against ~NZ$2.0m/year burn) is exhausted absent successful further financing.

base.equity_value_note: = (FY2026 shareholders' equity NZ$16,977,146 - CGU carrying value NZ$15,583,116) + CGU carrying value x (1 - 40% haircut) = NZ$1,394,030 + NZ$9,349,870 = NZ$10,743,900.
base.methodology: intrinsic_value = (FY2026 equity with 40%-haircut CGU) / shares diluted forward through the base-case 5-year capital-raise path = 10,743,900 / 1,367,632,036 = NZ$0.007858/share.

bull.methodology: intrinsic_value = (EV/oz resource value + net cash) / shares diluted forward through the lighter bull-case 2-year raise path = 25,221,425 / 1,003,583,679 = NZ$0.025131/share. This is the ONLY one of the three scenarios that lands materially above the current price, and it requires the narrow-vein execution problems that undermined FY2026 to actually be resolved - an outcome not yet demonstrated.

bear.equity_value_note: = (CGU carrying value NZ$15,583,116 x 10% forced-liquidation recovery) + cash NZ$1,176,627 - total debt NZ$93,133 - other liabilities NZ$824,764 - wind-down costs NZ$400,000 = NZ$1,417,042.
bear.methodology: intrinsic_value = residual equity after forced-liquidation CGU recovery, debt, other liabilities and wind-down costs / current share count (no further dilution assumed once failure crystallizes) = 1,417,042 / 793,346,782 = NZ$0.001786/share.

entry_price.not_meaningful_note: A standard 15%-IRR entry-price formula assumes a cash-generating asset whose interim distributions plus a fair-value exit can be discounted back to a purchase price. NTL.NZ generates no distributable cash flow (owner FCF negative in all 9 disclosed fiscal years), pays no dividends, and its 'exit value' in every scenario is either a forced-liquidation residual (bear), a haircut-book-value claim diluted by ongoing dilutive financing (base), or a speculative, unpriced resource-conversion outcome contingent on solving execution problems that have not yet been solved (bull). Consistent with the AFC.NZ/BGI.NZ precedent, this section reports the probability-weighted intrinsic value itself as the decision-useful 'entry price.'

recommended_entry_price.note: For this non-cash-flowing, going-concern-risk explorer, the decision-useful 'entry price' is the probability-weighted fair value (see probability_weighted.weighted_iv) - the maximum price a rational buyer should pay given the realistic scenario mix, since no IRR-hurdle cash-flow mechanics apply. This is roughly 11% below the current NZ$0.009 market price.

sensitivity.description: A standard WACC / terminal-growth grid is not meaningful here (no cash-flow stream exists to discount). Instead this matrix sensitizes the base-case intrinsic value to (rows) the haircut applied to the Talisman Mine CGU carrying value - reflecting the range of possible outcomes given the auditor's inability to verify its recoverable amount - and (columns) the cumulative 5-year dilution multiple from continued capital raises.
sensitivity.dilution_multiple_note: 1.0x = no further dilution; 1.72x = base-case 5-year path (18/15/12/8/5%); 2.2x = heavier ongoing dilution consistent with the company's own disclosed dependency on further capital with no committed source.
sensitivity.matrix_read_note: Row = CGU haircut (0% = full NZ$15,583,116 book value credited, i.e. the auditor's inability to verify recoverability is ignored entirely; 100% = the CGU assumed entirely unrecoverable, the most conservative read of a disclaimer of opinion). Column = cumulative dilution multiple. The current NZ$0.009 price sits within the matrix at low-haircut/low-dilution combinations (e.g. 0% haircut + 1.5x dilution = NZ$0.0143, or 25% haircut + 1.0x dilution = NZ$0.0165) but falls outside it at the more probable combinations toward the matrix centre and lower-right, where most of the probability-weighted outcome space sits.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear is weighted just under half (40%) given: (1) a second consecutive FULL DISCLAIMER OF OPINION - the auditor could not even form a view on whether the company's dominant asset (92% of book equity) is recoverable, a materially more severe finding than a going-concern emphasis-of-matter; (2) FY2026 cash of only NZ$1,176,627 against annual operating cash outflow of ~NZ$2.0m, implying under 8 months of self-funded runway absent a further raise; (3) a demonstrated, not merely hypothetical, execution failure - FY2026's actual production results (lower-than-planned concentrate grade, only ~10m of reef drivage mined against plan, development paused entirely at Mystery) show the core operating thesis has already been tested once and has not yet worked; (4) NO quantitative production or revenue guidance has been issued for FY2027, only a qualitative 'pause and reassess' plan, which is consistent with a company that does not currently have a credible near-term path to positive cash flow; and (5) explicit management disclosure that 'no assurance can be given that such [further] capital will be available at all or on terms acceptable to the Company.' Base (45%) is the modal outcome and reflects that NTL.NZ has, unlike a typical failed junior, successfully raised capital in EVERY year of an 8-year history without yet failing outright (shares grew from ~625m Sep-2024 to ~793m Mar-2026 via multiple completed raises, including a 33%-oversubscribed FY2023 rights issue) - continued dilutive survival, without near-term profitability, is the single most probable path given this unbroken track record of successfully finding new capital even through repeated operational disappointments. Bull (15%) reflects genuine, non-zero optionality on the underlying 350,000 oz AuEq JORC resource, a real (if high-grade-variable) historical endowment in a goldfield that hosts OceanaGold's profitable, currently-expanding Waihi operation nearby, PLUS tangible progress already made (plant commissioned, offtake agreements signed, first concentrate actually shipped) that distinguishes this from a pure pre-production explorer - but is held to a minority weight because the one full year of live production data (FY2026) demonstrated the execution risk crystallizing rather than resolving, and management's own FY2027 guidance is a strategic RESET (pause development, redo the geology) rather than a scale-up plan.

sanity_check.current_price_pb_note: At the current NZ$0.009 price, market cap is ~NZ$7.14m against FY2026 shareholders' equity of NZ$16,977,146 - an implied Price/Book of only ~0.42x, i.e. the market is ALREADY pricing in a substantial haircut to reported book value, consistent with (not contradicted by) the auditor's disclaimer of opinion on the dominant CGU asset. This is the opposite pattern from AFC.NZ/BGI.NZ, where the market persistently paid a PREMIUM to book for shell/RTO optionality; here the market is already applying a discount for genuine going-concern and asset-recoverability risk.
trip_reasons: The probability-weighted intrinsic value (NZ$0.00802) sits close to, but modestly below (-10.9%), the current market price (NZ$0.009) - a materially different result from the AFC.NZ/BGI.NZ precedents where every non-bull scenario was tens of percent below price; here the market's existing ~0.42x P/B discount already embeds much of the going-concern/CGU-recoverability risk this model separately quantifies.

Base and bear scenarios (NZ$0.00786 and NZ$0.00179) both sit below the current price, while bull (NZ$0.02513) sits well above it - the market price of NZ$0.009 falls between the base and bull cases, roughly consistent with the market assigning some material chance to a successful outcome without being priced for the bull case outright.

The bull-case EV/oz assumption (US$40/oz on an unreserved, JORC-resource-only, narrow-vein deposit with one year of disappointing live production data) is inherently judgmental; a reasonable analyst could argue for a lower multiple (US$20-25/oz, more typical of a pre-reserve explorer that has not yet demonstrated it can hit its own production plan), which would pull the bull case and the weighted IV down further.

The FY2026 disclaimer of opinion means the FY2026 shareholders' equity anchor used in the base and (to a lesser extent) bear cases is itself not fully independently verified - this model applies its own haircuts rather than relying on unadjusted book value, but the underlying uncertainty is real and not fully resolvable from public disclosure alone.
sanity_check.diagnosis: market price and model converge reasonably closely (within ~11%), unlike the AFC.NZ/BGI.NZ shell precedents where market price diverged sharply from fundamentals; NTL.NZ's ~0.42x P/B already reflects meaningful going-concern discounting by the market, and the residual gap here is a judgment call on the CGU haircut and bull-case resource multiple, not evidence of a mispriced shell
sanity_check.fix_applied: asset/scenario-weighted valuation instead of growth DCF, given no positive-FCF history exists and the CGU carrying value is the subject of an unresolved audit disclaimer

valuation_philosophy.no_positive_fcf_history: Free cash flow has been negative in every one of the 9 disclosed fiscal years (FY2018-FY2026), including FY2026, the first year with any meaningful production revenue at all (NZ$52,790, insufficient to cover the ~NZ$2.27m of operating and admin costs). There is no positive FCF year, in any period, to establish a base or a trend to project forward. A conventional owner-FCF DCF applied to this series would either extrapolate a business that has never existed (sustained positive cash generation) or compound the historical burn rate into a meaningless, ever-more-negative terminal value. That is why this model abandons the FCF-projection framework in favour of a probability-weighted asset/scenario approach.
valuation_philosophy.going_concern: The FY2026 audited financial statements (Baker Tilly Staples Rodway, 29 June 2026) contain a FULL DISCLAIMER OF OPINION - the second consecutive year - because the auditor could not obtain sufficient evidence on the recoverable amount of the NZ$15,583,116 Talisman Mine cash-generating unit, which represents roughly 92% of total shareholders' equity. The company has a low cash balance (NZ$1,176,627) relative to its ongoing cash demand (operating cash outflow of ~NZ$1,967,666 in FY2026 alone), and management explicitly states that further capital will be required with no assurance it will be obtained on acceptable terms, if at all.
valuation_philosophy.asset_optionality_distinguishes_this_fro: Unlike the AFC.NZ and BGI.NZ precedents in this research folder - both dormant cash shells with no meaningful operating assets, whose value rests almost entirely on listed-shell scarcity/RTO-option value - NTL.NZ holds a genuine, JORC-classified 350,000 oz gold-equivalent resource at an average grade of ~17 g/t in a historically rich goldfield (Karangahake, part of the Hauraki Goldfield that also hosts OceanaGold's profitable Waihi mine), a commissioned gravity-separation processing plant, and signed offtake agreements with two counterparties. This is why the bull case here is built on a resource-based EV/oz valuation of a real, disclosed asset, rather than the pure listed-shell-precedent figure used in the AFC.NZ/BGI.NZ bull cases - but it does not change the fundamental conclusion that no cash-flow-discounting framework applies, because the pathway from resource to sustained positive cash flow remains unproven (FY2026 was the one live test, and it fell short of plan).
valuation_philosophy.value_rests_on_execution_and_continued_d: The dominant driver of outcome dispersion in this model is not gold price or macro (both are genuinely supportive tailwinds, per the Analysis JSON's macro_factors) but company-specific execution risk (can narrow-vein mining be predicted and scaled) layered on financing risk (will the market keep funding an unbroken 8-year pattern of capital raises). The base case explicitly assumes BOTH that further dilutive capital continues to be available (as it has, without exception, for 8 years) AND that production does not durably scale within the horizon - i.e. survival without success. The bear case assumes financing or execution finally fails. The bull case assumes execution is finally solved.
valuation_philosophy.market_price_already_discounts_meaningfu: At the current NZ$0.009 price, the implied Price/Book is only ~0.42x - the market is already pricing in substantial risk to the reported book value, unlike the AFC.NZ/BGI.NZ shells where the market persistently paid a premium to book. The probability-weighted intrinsic value here (NZ$0.00802) sits only ~11% below the current price, meaningfully closer to fair value than the AFC.NZ/BGI.NZ precedents - this is a genuinely two-sided, high-variance situation (bear NZ$0.0018 to bull NZ$0.0251, a ~14x range) rather than a case of an obviously mispriced shell.
valuation_philosophy.uninvestable_at_current_price_conclusion: NTL.NZ is not obviously mispriced at the current NZ$0.009, but it is a binary, going-concern-risk bet whose modal (most probable, base-case) outcome is continued dilutive survival without near-term profitability (NZ$0.00786/share, -12.7% vs. current price), with a meaningful (40%) chance of an outright failure/wind-down outcome (NZ$0.0018/share, -80.2%) that materially outweighs the 15%-weighted bull-case upside (NZ$0.0251/share, +179.2%) in probability terms, even though the bull case's magnitude is large. A rational holder is compensated for real optionality on a genuine resource, but is also carrying real, audited going-concern and asset-recoverability risk that the second consecutive disclaimer of opinion makes explicit rather than speculative.
